about.followAlong.title: Follow-along
about.followAlong.description: This mode highlights the word being recited and colours where tajweed rules apply. A listening and learning aid only: it is not for correcting recitation, does not use artificial intelligence, and does not measure performance.
about.followAlong.hafs: It works with recitations that publish word-level timings, and with Hafs an Asim only. Today that means Quran Foundation and the twelve audited MP3Quran v4 recitations. Anything else still plays; the line just does not appear.
settings.followAlongAvailabilityHafs: Hafs an Asim only, for now.
settings.followAlongAvailabilityProvider: Quran Foundation recitations and the twelve audited MP3Quran v4 recitations.
settings.followAlongAvailabilityText: Quran text in the Uthmani script from Tanzil, verbatim.
settings.followAlongAvailabilityDataset: Ahkam data from quran-tajweed, under CC BY 4.0.
about.followAlong.accuracy: Accuracy is not total: word timings cover 99.45% of words in the supported Quran Foundation recitations and 99.99% in the twelve audited MP3Quran v4 recitations. In 0.70% of ayat fewer than 85% of the words are timed, so word tracking stops for that ayah and the whole ayah is highlighted until the next one starts, rather than lighting the wrong word. The app only synchronises the interface; the figures are computed from the published data.
about.followAlong.method: The colours mark where a rule applies in the text, not whether it was applied correctly. The mode does not record your voice, compare it, or give a verdict.
about.followAlong.licenseNote: Text under CC BY 3.0 with Tanzil terms, tajweed under CC BY 4.0, ayah markers under OFL.
site.title: Dhikr · Quran recitations with the mushaf
hero.title: An open Quran library
hero.body: A collection of Quran recitations and digital resources, for listening, reading and research.
tools.title: Open data and tools
tools.body: For listeners, teachers, researchers and developers: timings, recitations and Qalun text, on the ayah borders of the Jamahiriya mushaf.
tools.ayahTimingsBody: A file per surah for every reciter: when each ayah starts and ends, in milliseconds, for 37 reciters, on the Qalun ayah boundaries.
tools.wordTimingsBody: When each word of the recitation starts and ends, for 30 reciters so far.
tools.textBody: The whole text as in the Jamahiriya mushaf: 6,214 ayahs in 114 surahs, with its juz, hizb and eighths.
tools.apiBody: A JSON API for reciters, surahs, audio links and timings, with a free personal key for every developer.
tools.converterBody: Converts an ayah number between Hafs and Qalun numbering, both ways: Al-Baqara 286 in Hafs is 285 in Qalun.
tools.audioBody: Every surah of every reciter as MP3, or the whole khatma as one ZIP or as separate files.

about.reciter.title: The reciter page
about.reciter.body: Every reciter has a page that gathers all his surahs, to listen to or download. As he recites, the ayah being recited lights up, and in most recitations the word itself lights up, word by word, on the printed ink of the Jamahiriya mushaf. Where a recitation has no word timings, the whole ayah lights up.
about.mushaf.title: The mushaf
about.mushaf.body: The Quran text on Dhikr is the ink of the Jamahiriya mushaf as printed, in the riwaya of Qalun from Nafi, not a computer font.
about.data.title: Data and tools
about.data.body: The timing of every ayah of every recitation, the timing of every word for most of them, and an API for the list of reciters and recitations, all open to researchers and developers. More tools are being prepared.
about.sources.title: Where the recitations come from
about.sources.body: The recitations were gathered from public sources, among them Zuwara Quran Radio, the Libyan Quran TV channel, the Internet Archive and Way2Quran.

tools.ayahTimingsIdea: So any app can follow a recitation ayah by ayah: highlight the ayah being read, repeat it to memorise, or cut a passage, without anyone listening through the whole recitation to time it by hand.
tools.wordTimingsIdea: It is what lights each word in the mushaf here as it is recited. We want it in the hands of every teacher and developer, to build word-by-word teaching and memorisation on.
tools.textIdea: Most digital Quran texts follow Hafs and the Kufan count. This is the Qalun text with the later Madinan count, for whoever serves readers in Libya and the Maghreb.
tools.apiIdea: What Dhikr itself runs on is open to others, so a mosque website or a memorisation app can build on the same data instead of collecting it again.
tools.converterIdea: Most tafsirs and translations are numbered for Hafs; the converter links them to the right ayah in the Qalun mushaf, with no drift.
tools.audioIdea: For listening offline, and for radio stations and mosques that broadcast recitation: the same files people hear here.
cta.title: Build on Dhikr
cta.body: A free personal key for the API: reciters, surahs, and the timing of every ayah and every word, in the Qalun narration.
privacy.s1.title: In short
privacy.s1.body: Listening, reading and downloading a single surah need no account, and we do not know who you are when you do them. We keep personal data only if you create an account, and with an account we log API use and khatma downloads to know what is used and improve it. Dhikr is free: it sells nothing, shows no ads and sells no one's data.
privacy.s2.title: Without an account
privacy.s2.body:
Your place in a recitation, the appearance, and whether the mushaf is shown: kept in your browser only, never sent to us.
Copies of pages and files are kept in your browser so the site works offline.
A short mushaf session (a cookie named rdr) protects the mushaf images from automated copying; it carries neither your name nor your email. The mushaf images carry a hidden mark tied to that session, so a leaked image can be traced.
Ordinary server logs (IP address, page, time) are kept briefly, for security only.
privacy.s3.title: If you create an account
privacy.s3.body:
Your name and email address, your profile picture if you sign in with Google, and when the account was created.
API keys: we keep a fingerprint of each key, not the key itself, so we cannot show it again after it is made.
A session cookie keeps you signed in until you sign out, or for ninety days at most.
privacy.s4.title: What we log with your account
privacy.s4.body:
Every API request: the address requested, the time, the approximate country as Cloudflare estimates it, and the size and duration of the response.
Every download of a khatma or of picked surahs: the reciter, the number of surahs, the size, the country and the time.
We do not keep IP addresses in these logs. They exist to give real numbers about what is used, so we can improve Dhikr and know who builds on it.
privacy.s5.title: Services we rely on
privacy.s5.body:
Google: when you choose to sign in with it, it gives us only your name, email and picture.
Cloudflare: site visits and audio files pass through it; it counts the requests behind the listening figures, and checks that the email form is sent by a person (Turnstile).
Our own server: keeps the accounts and logs, and sends the sign-in email from no-reply@dhikr.ly.
We use no third-party analytics, advertising or tracking tools.
privacy.s6.title: Keeping and deleting
privacy.s6.body: We keep your account until you ask for it to be deleted, and delete its keys and everything logged under it with it. You can delete any key yourself from your account page at any time; to delete the whole account, write to us from the contact page.
privacy.s7.title: Security
privacy.s7.body: Connections to the site are encrypted, accounts live on our own server rather than with a third party, keys are stored as fingerprints rather than text, and an email sign-in link works once, within ten minutes.
privacy.s8.title: Changes and contact
privacy.s8.body: If anything here changes, we update this page and its date. For any question about your privacy, write to us from the contact page.
